def solve(nested):
    res=[]
    stack=[nested] if isinstance(nested,(list,tuple)) else [nested]
    # iterative to avoid recursion limits; need to process in order
    # Use list as stack of iterators
    # Simpler: recursive with explicit stack
    out=[]
    st=[(nested,0)] if isinstance(nested,(list,tuple)) else None
    if st is None:
        return [nested]
    # use explicit stack of (list_obj, index)
    # to avoid recursion depth issues
    stack=[(nested,0)]
    while stack:
        lst,idx=stack[-1]
        if idx>=len(lst):
            stack.pop()
            continue
        stack[-1]=(lst,idx+1)
        v=lst[idx]
        if isinstance(v,(list,tuple)):
            stack.append((v,0))
        else:
            out.append(v)
    return out

def solve(a, b):
    # Myers bit-parallel Levenshtein (exact, fast for long strings)
    if a == b:
        return 0
    # make a the shorter (pattern) to keep bit-vectors small
    if len(a) > len(b):
        a, b = b, a
    m = len(a)
    n = len(b)
    if m == 0:
        return n
    peq = {}
    for i, ch in enumerate(a):
        peq[ch] = peq.get(ch, 0) | (1 << i)
    vp = (1 << m) - 1
    vn = 0
    score = m
    top = 1 << (m - 1)
    mask_all = (1 << m) - 1
    for ch in b:
        eq = peq.get(ch, 0)
        xv = eq | vn
        xh = (((eq & vp) + vp) ^ vp) | eq
        ph = vn | (~(xh | vp) & mask_all)
        mh = vp & xh
        if ph & top:
            score += 1
        if mh & top:
            score -= 1
        ph = ((ph << 1) | 1) & mask_all
        mh = (mh << 1) & mask_all
        vp = (mh | (~(xv | ph) & mask_all)) & mask_all
        vn = (ph & xv) & mask_all
    return score
